1g_memoryless.definition: (u, c) reset to (STM, LTM) before every step; the network's own read-out summed over steps

1g_truncation_vs_windowed_bayes.definition:
an6: reservoir-memory truncation vs windowed Bayes, paired on the same episodes (XPOOL 48,000-59,999).
Truncated network (as esn_measure/m2 'start'): the state at step t is the LSTM run over only the last w read-in outputs
x_{t-w+1..t}, from the start state (STM, LTM); for t <= w the intact state (the window covers the whole history);
the network's own read-out on every step, summed. w = 1 is the memoryless reservoir.
Windowed Bayes with window w: Delta^(w)_t = LSE_k sum_{s=t-w+1..t} l_s - LSE_k sum_{s=t-w+1..t-1} l_s (uniform before the
window), summed over steps. Reported: T=30 accuracy of both for each w and the paired difference (mean, s.e.).
usage: an6.py NET [N]

definition.increments: d_t(j) = network per-step output for latent g (read-out applied to u_t), centred over j; parts N,W,M of Bayes's increment Delta_t = N+W+M (theory_marg/a1 definitions), centred over j; pooled over both latents as goal, episodes, steps in the range, values j. beta: multiple-regression coefficients (no intercept; all centred). R2_split_pratt: beta_k Cov(x_k,d)/Var(d), sums to R2. r_split_additive: Cov(d,part)/(sd(d) sd(Delta)), sums to r(d,Delta).
definition.episode_dependent: the same after subtracting each quantity's mean over episodes at each (step, value)
definition.cumulative: centred cumulative goal logits at t regressed on the cumulative parts
definition.fixed_goal_logits: F_t(j) = mean over episodes of the centred cumulative logits (= W M_t + t c, centred, for a linear read-out); Bayes's fixed part = mean over episodes of its centred log goal marginal; episode part = L - F
definition.memoryless: (u, c) reset to (STM, LTM) before every step; the network's own read-out summed over steps

1f_window_bayes.definition:
an3 (numpy; uses an1's saved per-step logits). Windowed Bayes: the update with the other latent averaged under the
posterior of only the last w-1 observations (uniform before them):
    Delta^(w)_t(j) = LSE_k Lambda_{t,w}(j,k) - LSE_k Lambda_{t-1,w-1}(j,k),  Lambda_{t,w} = sum_{s=t-w+1..t} l_s(j,k)
w = 1 is the step-wise rule, w = 30 is Bayes. For each w: the rule's T=30 accuracy (sum of its increments), and how
well each network's per-step goal increments d_t(j) (centred) are fitted by a * Delta^(w)_t (one scale a; pooled over
both latents as goal, episodes, steps 2-30, values), and the cumulative logits at T=30 by a * sum_t Delta^(w)_t.
Also the memoryless network outputs (state reset before every step) against w = 1.
XPOOL episodes 48,000-59,999 (an1's set).

E55.definition_hybrid: u_hyb_t = F(x_t; s_ref_{t-1}) + J_s(ref) (s_hyb_{t-1} - s_ref_{t-1}): the exact nonlinear one-step response to the current input from the reference state plus the linear propagation of the history deviation; removes only the reservoir's history x current-input interaction. interaction share = sum|u - u_hyb|^2 / sum|u - u_ref|^2
E55.definition: u_lin = u_ref + du, du from the LSTM step's Jacobian along the reference trajectory driven by the per-step mean read-in output xbar_t from the start state; nonlinear share = sum|u - u_lin|^2 / sum|u - u_ref|^2

R1e5.definition_hybrid: u_hyb_t = F(x_t; s_ref_{t-1}) + J_s(ref) (s_hyb_{t-1} - s_ref_{t-1}): the exact nonlinear one-step response to the current input from the reference state plus the linear propagation of the history deviation; removes only the reservoir's history x current-input interaction. interaction share = sum|u - u_hyb|^2 / sum|u - u_ref|^2
R1e5.definition: u_lin = u_ref + du, du from the LSTM step's Jacobian along the reference trajectory driven by the per-step mean read-in output xbar_t from the start state; nonlinear share = sum|u - u_lin|^2 / sum|u - u_ref|^2

LSTMe5.definition_hybrid: u_hyb_t = F(x_t; s_ref_{t-1}) + J_s(ref) (s_hyb_{t-1} - s_ref_{t-1}): the exact nonlinear one-step response to the current input from the reference state plus the linear propagation of the history deviation; removes only the reservoir's history x current-input interaction. interaction share = sum|u - u_hyb|^2 / sum|u - u_ref|^2
LSTMe5.definition: u_lin = u_ref + du, du from the LSTM step's Jacobian along the reference trajectory driven by the per-step mean read-in output xbar_t from the start state; nonlinear share = sum|u - u_lin|^2 / sum|u - u_ref|^2

1_lesions_and_linear_decoding.definitions:
an4 (forward passes only): where in the 5/5 rescue (E55) is the nonlinearity used? XPOOL episodes 48,000-51,999.
Lesions (each replaces one stage by its first-order Taylor expansion at a reference point; the rest is intact):
  readout_lin : per-step read-out MLP replaced by MLP(ubar_t) + J_t (u_t - ubar_t), ubar_t = mean state at step t
  readin_lin  : read-in MLP (incl. its final ReLU) replaced by its linearisation at the mean input [obar; zbar]
Linear decodability (ridge, one decoder shared across environments, train 3,000 / test 1,000 episodes, steps 2-30 pooled):
  from u_t: Bayes's increment Delta_t, the step-wise increment, the naive increment, the windowed (w=5) increment,
  for both latents (20 targets, each latent centred); the accuracy of the summed decoded Delta_t (a regression-fitted
  linear per-step read-out) for E55, R1e5, LSTMe5.
usage: an4.py

2_fixed_goal_logits.definitions:
an5 (numpy/torch CPU; uses an1's saved per-step logits on XPOOL 48,000-59,999). Is the networks' fixed
(episode-independent) goal-logit part a harmful prior?
  F^net_t(j)   = mean over episodes of the network's centred cumulative logits (per latent, step)
  F^naive_t(j), F^Bayes_t(j): the same for naive Bayes's and Bayes's centred log goal scores
(a) size: spread (max - min over j) and the episode part's RMS, per rule;
(b) scan: L' = L - (1 - kappa) F^net (kappa = 1 is the network): T=30 accuracy vs kappa;
(c) free offset: b(j) per latent and step fitted to minimise goal cross-entropy vs Bayes's goal marginal on episodes
    0-5,999 (convex in b), tested on 6,000-11,999: accuracy change at T=30 (and at t = 10).

3_readouts.definition: per-step read-outs on frozen states, logits summed over steps, marginal output, loss own, Adam lr 1e-3, batch 2000 fresh environments per update (no fixed pool), fp16 autocast; held-out curve on 16,000 fixed fresh episodes (seed 4242); final on 20,000 other fresh episodes (seed 999) with references; convergence = change over the last 20% of updates (paired, same held-out episodes); 'converged' if |d_acc| < 0.005 and the loss change is < 1% of the loss

1_step_index_decoding.definition:
an7: how much step-index (time since the start) information does a per-step state carry? (CPU, XPOOL)
Ridge decoder of the one-hot step index t from u_t (shared across environments; train 2,000 episodes, test 1,000);
accuracy of the argmax by step. For R1e5, E55, LSTMe5; u_t^ML (memoryless) carries none by construction.
This bounds what a per-step read-out on the real u_t can gain from the start-state transient rather than from
past inputs.

3_readout_parts_regression.definitions:
an8 (CPU): which parts of Bayes's update do the trained per-step read-outs on R1's frozen states capture?
Loads the read-outs from ckpt/<job>.pt; R1e5 states on XPOOL 48,000-59,999 (em_common fp32 replay; the read-outs were
trained on fp16-matmul states, max state difference ~4e-4); per-step increments d_t(j) (centred) regressed on Bayes's
naive / within-step / memory parts exactly as an1 (both latents as goal, steps 2-30), plus T=30 accuracy.
usage: an8.py JOB [JOB ...]

1_3_history_averaging_ablation.definitions:
an9 (CPU, WPOOL: 10 environments x 100 cells x 40 episodes): history-averaging ablation of a per-step read-out.
For a network's per-step goal output d_t(j) (read-out applied to its real state u_t), replace it by its average over all
episodes of the same environment with the same current bit pattern o_t at the same step t:
    dbar_t(j) = E[ d_t(j) | environment, o_t, t ]
dbar is a memoryless but step-aware rule built from the network's own outputs (no off-distribution states). Summing
dbar instead of d removes exactly what the outputs owe to the episode's history (past inputs, and through them the
cell), while keeping the current input, z, the step index and the operating point. Accuracy(d) - accuracy(dbar) is the
accuracy the read-out gets from history. Also: dbar pooled over steps (E[d | env, o_t]: removes the step index too).
Nets: R1e5's own read-out, the trained read-outs of job A (h2_u, h2_uml) and job B (h1_u), E55, LSTMe5.
usage: an9.py
